questions.q_en:
Select the option that expresses the following sentence in superlative degree of comparison.

He is a fast runner.
options_en: He is faster than any runner.
No other runner is as faster as he is.
questions.solution_en:
The adjective is 'fast' and it is in the positive degree, which means it does not show any comparison. To change a sentence from the positive degree to the superlative degree, we need to add -est to the adjective and use the definite article 'the' before it. The superlative degree shows that something or someone has the highest degree of quality among all the others in a group.

Hence, option (a) is the correct answer.

Option (b) is in comparative degree.

Option (c) is incorrect as 'faster' is in the comparative degree while the positive degree is used with 'as...as'.

Note:

Adjectives: Words which are used with a noun/pronoun to describe or point out, the person, animal, place, or thing which the noun names, or to tell the number or quantity, are called Adjectives.

· The Positive Degree is used to denote the mere existence of some quality of what we speak about. It is used when no comparison is made.

· The Comparative degree denotes a higher degree of quality than the positive and is used when two things are compared.

· The Superlative degree indicates the highest degree of quality and is used when more than two things (or sets of things) are compared.

questions.q_en:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in active voice.

The contract will have been signed by the partners by next Friday.
options_en: The partners will have signed the contract by next Friday.
The partners will sign the contract by next Friday.
The partners will be signing the contract by next Friday.
The partners would sign the contract by next Friday.
questions.solution_en:
The subject of the Passive Voice is changed into the object of the Active Voice. Also, the object of the Passive Voice is changed into the subject of the Active Voice.

The removal of the "to be" verb (been) and the preposition "by" is necessary while changing the voice of the sentence from Passive to Active.

The Passive voice in this question is in Future Perfect. Thus, the Active voice will also be in Future Perfect.

In Passive voice, the format is: Object of the Active voice (Subjective case) + will/shall + have + been + V3 + by + Subject of the Active voice (Objective case)

Thus, the format of Active voice is: Subject + will/shall + have + V3 + Object.

For example:

The gold will have been bought by her. (Passive Voice)

She will have bought the gold. (Active Voice)

The options except (a) don't follow the correct grammatical format of the Active Voice.

Therefore, the correct answer is: The partners will have signed the contract by next Friday.

Hence, (a) is the correct answer.

questions.q_en:
In the following question, a sentence has been given in Direct/Indirect speech. Out of the four alternatives suggested, select the one which best expresses the same sentence in Indirect/Direct speech.

Hema said to her mother, “I am going to buy some books for my exam”.
options_en: Hema told her mother that she was gone to buy some books for my exam.
Hema said to her mother that if she was to go to buy some books for her exam.
Hema told her mother that she was going to buy some books for her exam.
Hema told her mother that she had been going to buy some books for her exam.
questions.solution_en:
The sentence in the Direct Speech is in Present Continuous Tense. Therefore, the sentence in the Indirect Speech should be in Past Continuous Tense.

Present Continuous (Subject + is/am/are + V1 + ing + Object) should be converted into Past Continuous (Subject + was/were + V1 + ing + Object).

For example:

He said, I am checking the assignment. (Direct Speech)

He said that he was checking the assignment. (Indirect Speech)

The following things in the sentence should change when changed from Direct speech to Indirect Speech:

‘I’ changes into ‘she’. Change ‘said to’ into ‘told’."

Therefore, the correct answer is option (c).

questions.q_en:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in indirect speech.

My brother said to me, "Don't play in the rain."
options_en: My brother said to me don't play in the rain.
My brother forbade me to play in the rain.
My brother assured me not to play in the rain.
My brother refused me to not play in the rain.
questions.solution_en:
Imperative Sentences sometimes begin with Negative Commands like "Don't".

The reporting verbs like "said/say", etc. are changed into "asked/ask", "told/tell", "advised/ advise" etc.

"Not + To + V1" is used in these sentences. For example, "don't go" should be changed to "not to go" in Indirect speech.

In this context, "Don't ......" changes into "not to ......".

For example:

My friend said to me, "Don't go to Kolkata." (Direct Speech)

My friend advised me not to go to Kolkata. (Indirect Speech)

The following things in the sentence should change when changed from Direct speech to Indirect Speech:

'Said to me' would be changed to 'forbade me'.

'Don't' would be deleted and simply replaced with 'to' since forbade in itself is negative in nature.

Therefore, the correct answer is option (b): My brother forbade me to play in the rain.

questions.q_en: Select the sentence that is expressed in passive voice.
options_en: The results are announced by the principal.
They are planning a surprise party.
questions.solution_en:
Option (a): This sentence is in passive voice.

The subject ("results") is receiving the action ("are announced"), and the doer ("principal") is introduced with "by."

Hence, option (a) is the answer.

Option (b): This sentence is in active voice. The subject ("They") performs the action ("are planning").

Option (c): This sentence is in active voice. The subject ("She") performs the action ("cleaned").

Option (d): This sentence is in active voice. The subject ("He") performs the action ("organize").

Note: Active and Passive Voice: When the person doing the action is the subject, the sentence is said to be in active form/voice. When the subject is what the action is directed at, then the sentence is said to be in passive form/voice. For example: Active Voice: Rita and her friends performed a skit. Here 'Rita and her friends' (subject) perform the action. Passive Voice: A skit was performed by Rita and her friends. Here 'skit' is the subject (at which the action is directed).

questions.q_en:
Spot the erroneous part if any, in the following sentence.

The collection of/ vintage coins were(A)/ meticulously curated, / featuring rare pieces from(B)/ various historical periods/ and regions around the world(C). / No error (D).
questions.solution_en:
The error here is related to subject-verb agreement. The subject of this sentence is "the collection," which is a singular noun. However, the verb used in this sentence is "were," which is the plural form of the verb "to be." This is incorrect because the subject "the collection" is singular, so the verb should also be singular. To correct this error, we should use the singular form of the verb "to be," which is "was". Hence, (a) is the correct answer.

The final sentence: The collection of vintage coins was meticulously curated, featuring rare pieces from various historical periods and regions around the world.

Note: Subject-Verb Agreement: Matching up singular or plural subjects with singular or plural forms of a verb is part of the process called agreement. This can be understood better by the examples given: - "She likes cooking." [singular subject and verb] -- "They like to cook vegetables." [plural subject and verb]

The given sentence is divided into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.

A company can / make money by / obtain resources / more affordably.
questions.solution_en:
The error lies in the segment "obtain resources." When the preposition "by" is followed by a verb to indicate the means of achieving something, the verb should be in the gerund form (verb + -ing). The correct phrase is "obtaining resources," as the gerund is required after "by."

· Option 1 ("A company can") is correct as the subject and modal verb.

· Option 2 ("make money by") is correct, setting up the gerund requirement.

· Option 3 ("obtain resources") should be "obtaining resources."

· Option 4 ("more affordably") is correct as a comparative adverb.

Thus, the segment with the error is obtain resources.

questions.q_en: Select the option with the correct use of the past perfect tense.
options_en: I was living in this city for five years before I moved to the countryside.
I lived in this city for five years before I moved to the countryside.
I had living in this city for five years before I moved to the countryside.
I had lived in this city for five years before I moved to the countryside.
questions.solution_en:
The past perfect tense is used to talk about an action that happened before another action in the past. In this sentence, the action "had lived in the city" occurred before the action "moved to the countryside".

Option (a)- This uses the past continuous tense, which is incorrect in this context.

Option (b)- This uses the simple past tense, which is incorrect in this context.

Option (c) - This uses the past perfect tense in partially correct form, as the verb "live" should be in the past participle form "lived" instead of the -ing form "living", and the form should be "had lived" instead of "had living".

Hence, the correct answer is option (d).

Note:

Participle: A word formed from a verb (e.g. going, gone, being, been) and used as an adjective (e.g. working woman, burnt toast) or a noun (e.g. good breeding). In English, participles are also used to make compound verb forms (e.g. is going, has been). Consider the sentences given below:

Dancing at the party, the women fell on the ground.

Encouraged by her parents, Rita went on to pursue her passion.

The highlighted word in the first sentence is of the form Verb + ing and is used as a present participle. It is used to denote an action that is going on or incomplete or imperfect.

The highlighted word in the second sentence is of the form verb + ed. It is used as a past participle. It denotes the completed action or state of the thing spoken of.

A past participle ends with the following: -ed, -d, -t, -en, or -n.

One should take great care and never get confused between a gerund and a present participle. They use the same forms but perform different functions: a gerund is a verbal noun, while a present participle is a verbal adjective.

questions.solution_en:

The subject "I" pairs with the base form of the verb "pick" in the simple present tense, not "picks" (which is used for third-person singular subjects).

Option 1 corrects the verb to "pick," making it grammatically correct: "I always pick."

Option 2 uses "is picking," which is present continuous and unsuitable for habitual actions.

Option 3 uses "picked," which is past tense and does not match the context of a general habit.

Option 4 uses "picking," which is a gerund/participle and grammatically incorrect here.

Thus, the correct option is 1: "Between two evils, I always pick the one I have never tried before."

Parts of a sentence are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the parts in the correct order to form a meaningful sentence.

a) several authors justify

b) the probability postulates

c) of sleeping pills without relying

d) on the arguments
questions.solution_en:
The opening part should be the one mentioned in 'a' as it talks about the opinion of authors. 'b-c' is a pair as 'b' talks of 'postulates' and the subject of postulates 'sleeping pills' is mentioned in 'c'. What these authors do not want to rely on is mentioned in 'd' which makes it the last part of the sentence.

The correct sequence of the part of sentence is a,b,c,d.

The sentence is - Several authors justify the probability postulates of sleeping pills without relying on the arguments.

Hence, option (d) is correct.

questions.q_en: Select the option with the correct use of the present tense.
options_en: She spended all her money on make-up in order to look beautiful.
She had spend all her money on make-up in order to look beautiful.
She spends all her money on make-up in order to look beautiful.
She has spend all her money on make-up in order to look beautiful.
questions.solution_en:
· "Spended" (Option 1) is incorrect because the past tense of "spend" is "spent", not "spended."

· "Had spend" (Option 2) is incorrect because after "had" (past perfect), the verb should be in the past participle ("spent" instead of "spend").

· "Has spend" (Option 4) is incorrect because after "has" (present perfect), the correct past participle form "spent" should be used instead of "spend."

· "Spends" (Option 3) is correct because it correctly follows the simple present tense rule (subject + verb in present form).

questions.q_en:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in active voice.

The guests shall be welcomed by the receptionist.
options_en: The receptionist will have welcomed the guests.
The receptionist shall welcome the guests.
The receptionist should welcome the guests.
The receptionist shall be welcoming the guests.
questions.solution_en:
The subject of the Passive Voice is changed into the object of the Active Voice. Also, the object of the Passive Voice is changed into the subject of the Active Voice.

The removal of the helping verb and the preposition 'by' is necessary while changing the voice of the sentence from Passive to Active.

These types of questions contain Modal verbs and they should be used correctly as stated below. Modal verbs can be identified by the following:

Can
Could
May
Might
Shall
Should
Will
Would

In Passive voice, the format is: Object of the Active voice (Subjective case) + Modal + be + V3 + by + Subject of the Active voice (Objective case).

Thus, the format of sentences containing Modal verbs in Active voice is: Subject + Modal + V1 + Object.

For example:

The issue shall be solved by you. (Passive Voice)

You shall solve the issue. (Active Voice)

From the given options, the sentence that follows the Active voice format is option (b), "The receptionist shall welcome the guests".

Hence, the correct answer is option (b).

questions.q_en:
Parts of a sentence are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the parts in the correct order to form a meaningful sentence.

A. her wild subjects with an open

B. degree in science, Goodall says she observed

C. a secretarial student without an undergraduate

D. mind and without preconceptions
questions.solution_en:
Parts CB make a pair and it describes the subject, 'Goodall'. This has to come first so that the remaining parts make a meaningful order. The pair is followed by part A which denotes the thing that the subject observes in the sentence and the manner in which she does is given in part D. So, it is the last part. Thus, the final order of the parts of the given sentence is CBAD.

The complete sentence is: A secretarial student without an undergraduate degree in science, Goodall says she observed her wild subjects with an open mind and without preconceptions.

Hence, the correct answer is option (a).
